manifest.name: dsh-mcp-manager
manifest.description: Manage MCP servers inside DeepSeek Harness: list, add, edit, remove, test, and switch them on or off per session.

bundle.text:
# dsh-mcp-manager bundle layer.
#
# One row owns the full MCP server list (volatile `servers`) and the browser
# pages that edit it and toggle servers per session. Each enabled server is
# mounted as a programmatic `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` instance, so its
# tools, resources, and instructions behave exactly like a profile-configured
# MCP row.
- insert:
    - id: mcp-manager
      name: dsh-mcp-manager
      config:
        servers: []

readme.text:
[](https://github.com/097794/dsh-mcp-manager/actions/workflows/test.yml)

Manage [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) from the Web UI:

- **Settings → MCP servers**: list, add, edit, remove, enable/disable and test servers.
- **Composer `+` menu → MCP servers**: turn any server on or off for the current session only.

Every configured server is mounted as a real `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` instance, so its tools (`mcp__<name>__<tool>`), resources, and server instructions behave exactly like a hand-written MCP row in the profile.

Requires a DSH build with the plugin system, e.g. DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 desktop.

1. Clone or copy this directory somewhere stable.
2. Install it as a profile bundle: **Plugins → Add plugin → local directory**, or the plugin manager tool's `install_bundle` with this folder's absolute path.
3. Keep the folder: a local-directory install is linked, not copied.

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Becomes the tool namespace `mcp__<name>__<tool>`. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, max 32. |
| Transport | `stdio` for a local program, `streamable-http` for a remote service. |
| Command / arguments / working directory | stdio only; one argument per line. |
| Environment | stdio only; `KEY=VALUE` per line. Values may use `${ENV_VAR}`. |
| URL / headers | streamable-http only; headers are `Name: Value` per line, `${ENV_VAR}` allowed. |
| Enabled | Off means no connection and no tools. |

Changes are staged as a draft and applied with **Save**. The host reconciles immediately: removed or edited servers are disconnected, new ones are connected.

**Test** mounts the server in an isolated scope and reports the tool count and names without touching the live tool list. `${ENV_VAR}` references are expanded from the harness process environment; a missing variable fails that server with a clear message.
Servers that already exist as MCP rows in the profile (for example a `mcp-anysearch` row) are listed read-only under **From the profile**; their tools still participate in per-session switches.

Open the composer's **+** menu (the same menu as `/` commands) and pick **MCP servers**. The same popup area that held the menu now shows the server list with tool counts and a switch per server:

- off → that server's tools are hidden from the agent (`tools.restrict` deny) and its `mcp:<name>` prompt section is dropped for this session;
- on → both come back.

Click outside or press Escape to close it, exactly like the command menu.
The state is a durable per-session plugin record (`plugin:mcp-manager/toggles`), so it survives reload and does not leak into other sessions. Subagents start with every server enabled.

- The host row owns one volatile `servers` config. `apply` mounts one child `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` plugin per enabled server with `ctx.plugin(...)`, so Cordis owns connection lifetime and disposal.
- `system-prompt/assemble` removes `mcp:<name>` sections for servers the session switched off.
- `agent/created`, `agent/disposed` and `tools/change` keep per-agent tool restrictions in sync; restrictions are recomputed as MCP tools appear or disappear.
- The browser half talks to a small same-origin JSON API (`/dsh-mcp-manager/api/...`) for status, tests, and session switches, renders its manager page as a `settings.section` page (Settings → MCP servers), and contributes a `/mcp` command whose action opens an overlay panel in `conversation.input.overlay` — the same anchor the composer popup menus use. It is unauthenticated like every other route on the loopback Web server — do not expose this host beyond loopback.

- Developed against **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2**. It relies on plugin-facing APIs (`ctx.plugin`, `tools.restrict`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `appendPluginRecord`) that are not a public compatibility promise.
- A stdio server command runs with the harness process's environment. Only add servers you trust.
- Tool hiding is per session and per agent; it is not a security boundary against the model calling a tool through another provider.
- Removing a server does not delete anything it wrote; it only disconnects it.

```sh
node --test test/model.test.mjs
```

`lib/model.js` is pure: server normalization, `${VAR}` expansion, MCP tool-name mapping, and the `dsh-mcp-client` config builder, all testable without a harness.
